title: Inference Readiness: cross-eval matrix and promotion playbook
author: Aditi Malhotra
body:
Summary:
This playbook defines the cross-cutting evaluation matrix and step-by-step promotion process we use to move a candidate model from onboarding to production serving in Redwood Inference. It consolidates responsibilities for functional correctness, latency/throughput contracts, quantization safety, prompt/benchmark coverage, and regression triage so product, infra, and applied-ML teams have a single canonical flow to follow.

Scope and goals:
- Scope: models intended for text generation, chat, and embeddings that will be served on Hosted or Dedicated tiers.
- Goals:
  - Ensure predictable user-facing latency and cost before promotion.
  - Verify semantic quality and safety across prioritized prompt sets.
  - Validate quantization profiles and KV-cache behaviour under representative workloads.
  - Provide a clear, repeatable rollback and regression-triage path.

Owner and stakeholders:
- Playbook owner: Applied ML Platform (responsibility: maintain checks and eval harness integration).
- Release owner: Model-product engineer (responsibility: execute promotion steps).
- Reviewers: SRE for latency/SLO approval, Security for data handling review, Eval team for prompt/quality acceptance.

Promotion gates (high level):
1) Functional acceptance (unit/eval harness): pass targeted task-level metrics on production prompt sets.
2) Latency & capacity contract: meet P95 latency target under steady-state and burst profiles.
3) Quantization & memory safety: have a validated quant profile with deterministic KV-cache behavior.
4) Safety & quality guardrails: no new critical safety regressions versus baseline.
5) Rollout plan and monitoring: instrumentation, alerts, and rollback criteria defined and verified.

Promotion matrix (example):
| Gate | Metric | Threshold | Artifact to attach | Approver |
| ---- | ------ | --------- | ------------------ | ------- |
| Functional | Top-line accuracy / utility (task dependent) | >= baseline - 1.5% absolute OR non-inferior within CI | eval-harness run-id + logs | Applied ML Platform |
| Latency | P95 tail latency (single-token) | <= 120ms hosted / <= 30ms dedicated | loadtest run + perf profile | SRE |
| Throughput | Sustained tokens/sec per GPU | >= expected for planned instance type | perf bench report | Serving Runtime |
| Quantization | Perplexity / semantic drift delta | <= 2% relative vs FP16 baseline | quant-eval report + weight-diff log | Applied ML Platform |
| Safety | Safety regression score (eval suite) | no critical regressions; <= permitted minor regressions | safety-eval bundle | Trust & Safety reviewer |

Evaluation pipeline (step-by-step):
1. Kickoff and artifact collection:
   - Create promotion ticket with model hash, docker image, config, target deployment mode, and list of prioritized prompt sets.
   - Attach model card, training data provenance summary, and initial eval-harness run.
2. Baseline comparison run:
   - Run eval-harness against canonical prompt sets (see Prompt selection below).
   - Collect deterministic seeds and randomization logs to enable replay.
3. Performance simulation:
   - Run the serving-simulation harness with representative workload profiles: steady-state, burst, long-context, and adversarial prompts.
   - Capture latency distributions (P50/P90/P95), memory growth over long-context, and KV-cache hit ratios.
4. Quantization validation:
   - Create quant profiles (INT8/4-bit variants) using the adaptive quant tuner.
   - Run per-workload quant-eval to check semantic delta and failure modes ( hallucination rate, tokenization mismatches).
   - Confirm goldens: 50 sample runs must be byte-for-byte identical for prefix-preserved sequences where expected.
5. Guardrails and safety evals:
   - Execute safety and red-team prompt sets; run the continuous-safety-eval pipeline for the candidate model.
   - Verify no new critical safety regressions and triage any minor failures with TODO action items.
6. Load and canary rehearsal:
   - Deploy to a staging fleet (1–5% footprint) under production traffic mirroring.
   - Verify monitoring: token-level cost, trace spans, tail latency, error rate.
7. Promotion decision and rollout plan:
   - If all gates green, schedule controlled rollout. Document rollout windows, incremental steps, and rollback triggers.

Prompt selection and benchmark design:
- Canonical prompt sets must include:
  - Core product prompts (derived from top 100 user flows).
  - Edge-case prompts (long-context, low-resource/ambiguous queries).
  - Safety & red-team prompts (policy-sensitive scenarios).
  - Transfer prompts for quantization sensitivity (prefix-heavy stateful conversations).
- For each prompt set include metadata: intent, expected tokens, complexity score, and weight for aggregated metrics.
- Benchmarking guidance: use stratified sampling across intent and length; maintain a public seed file for reproducibility.

Quantization profiles and KV-cache rules:
- For each deployment target (hosted, dedicated instance types) maintain a recommended quant profile label (e.g., q8-default, q4-aggressive).
- Validation checklist:
  - Apply quant profile, run functional and safety evals.
  - Run long-context KV-cache consistency test: repeated prefix + interleaved queries for 10k tokens and assert cache hit stability and bounded memory.
  - Record weight diffs and activation ranges; attach quant diagnostics.
- If quant causes >2% semantic drift on critical prompts, mark as "Requires manual review" and do not promote.

Quality guardrails and monitoring to provision before rollout:
- Required dashboards: per-route P95 latency, token-consumption per request, model-version error rate, safety-regression alert.
- Pre-deployment SLOs to confirm:
  - Latency: P95 <= threshold by deployment class.
  - Errors: 5xx rate < 0.1% over 24h during staging.
  - Cost-per-1k tokens within expected range +/- 15%.
- Alerts and automated mitigation:
  - Safety regression alert routes to on-call Trust & Safety and product owner.
  - Incremental traffic rebalancer: if P95 exceeds threshold for >10m, reduce traffic to candidate by 50% automatically.

Regression triage and post-failure protocol:
1. Detection: alert fires or user-reported regression.
2. Triage steps:
   - Reproduce with eval-harness using the failing prompt(s) and attached seeds.
   - Compare against previous release artifact (binary diff of logits and token probabilities for failing runs).
   - Classify failure: performance (latency/memory), semantic (quality), safety, or quantization-related.
3. Mitigation map:
   - Performance: rollback or reduce concurrency; file perf ticket to runtime team.
   - Semantic: revert to previous model or pin to safer quant profile, open triage with Applied ML.
   - Safety: immediate rollback, incident response with Trust & Safety.
4. RCA and prevention: publish postmortem, update prompt sets with new cases, and add guardrail rules to evaluation harness.

Rollout procedure (concrete steps):
1. Pre-window checklist (must be green): security review, monitoring hooks, runbook linked, rollback tested.
2. Canary (1% traffic, 30m): validate metrics and log sampling.
3. Ramp (5% -> 25% -> 50%): 30–60m between steps depending on stability.
4. Full cutover: switch traffic and maintain elevated monitoring for 24–72h.
5. Post-rollout: collect telemetry, confirm no regressions, and close promotion ticket.

Required artifacts for promotion ticket (attach as files or links):
- Model image and model hash.
- eval-harness run id and raw logs.
- perf bench reports and loadtest artifacts.
- quantization report and activation histograms.
- prompt-set definitions and seed files.
- Safety-eval reports and red-team notes.
- Rollout plan and runbook links.

Appendix: commonly used CLI snippets and JSON examples
- Run eval-harness (example):
```
redwood-eval run --model-image gcr.io/redwood/model:2026-01 --prompt-set canonical_v3 --output=run-12345
```
- Simple quant-eval config (example JSON):
```
{
  "model_hash": "sha256:abcdef..",
  "quant_profile": "q4-aggressive",
  "seed": 42,
  "prompt_sets": ["canonical_v3", "safety_v2"]
}
```
- Loadtest invocation (example):
```
perf-sim --target model-service-staging --profile steady-state-10k --duration 20m --out perf-report.json
```

Appendix: escalation contacts (on-call rotation)
- Applied ML Platform on-call: #applied-ml-oncall (PagerDuty)
- Serving runtime SRE: #runtime-oncall (PagerDuty)
- Trust & Safety emergency: trust-safety@redwood.com
